steps.name: Sample structure QC
caveats: If one sample has a library size several times below the median of the study, do not delete it in silence. Keep it through the sample structure QC, look at it on the PCA and on the sample distance heatmap, report its library size and its detected genes beside the others, and remove it only with a stated reason. The count models down-weight a low-depth sample through its size factor, thus removal is a judgment, not a default.

The counts are Salmon output as delivered and the record does not state whether the length correction occurred; for sample-structure QC on library size, PCA, and distances this does not change the conclusion, but flag it for any later differential expression plan (import_state = unknown).
steps.context: Bulk RNA-seq, human skin, 12 samples in two conditions (6 AD lesional treated vs 6 control), unpaired, single batch, raw gene-level Salmon counts (length-correction status unstated in the profile). Data: /eval-four-models-v2-with-qc-only-n6-s1-1/data/inputs/counts/counts.csv (12000 genes x 13 columns) and /eval-four-models-v2-with-qc-only-n6-s1-1/data/inputs/metadata/metadata.csv (12 x 2). Known flag: sample_01 has a library size about 4x below the median. DESeq2 1.52.0 is installed.
steps.question: Before any test: what do the library sizes, a PCA on the 500 most variable genes, and the sample-to-sample distances say about the 6 AD lesional treated vs 6 control samples, and is sample_01 (library size ~4x below the median) defective enough to exclude?

grounding.reason: Sample structure QC: vst(blind), PCA on 500 top-variance genes, sample distance heatmap, library sizes per R-0033@40bf, with the low-depth sample kept and reported per R-0008@440d

constraints: transform = vst_blind: varianceStabilizingTransformation with blind=TRUE before the design is informed (vignette:DESeq2/1.52.0#blind-dispersion-estimation)

low_depth_policy = keep_inspect_report: keep sample_01 through the QC, inspect it on the PCA and distance heatmap, report its library size and detected genes beside the others, remove only with a stated reason (doi:10.1186/s13059-016-0881-8)
Run the sample structure QC on the raw counts before any model-based testing; no differential expression or enrichment step in this plan
steps.description: Read the 12000 x 13 Salmon gene-level count matrix (counts.csv; first column gene identifiers, remaining 12 columns samples) and the 12 x 2 metadata table (metadata.csv; condition = treated/control), verify sample IDs align between the two files, then: (1) report per-sample library size (column sums), DESeq2 size factors, and number of genes detected above a low-count threshold, as a table; (2) fit a DESeq2 design ~ condition, apply varianceStabilizingTransformation with blind=TRUE, compute PCA on the 500 genes with the highest variance and plot PC1 vs PC2 colored by condition (label sample_01 explicitly); (3) compute the Euclidean distance matrix between samples on the vst values and draw a sample-distance heatmap annotated by condition; (4) give a verdict on sample_01: its library size and detected genes beside the other 11, its position on the PCA and distance heatmap, and an explicit keep (default) or remove recommendation with a stated reason. Report whether the primary axis of variance separates treated from control and whether any sample departs from its group. No differential expression or enrichment runs in this plan.
acceptance_criteria: A per-sample table covering all 12 samples with library size, size factor, and detected-gene count, with sample_01 values contrasted against the other samples and against the median
A PCA plot on the 500 top-variance genes from blind vst values, colored by condition, with the share of variance explained by PC1 and PC2 stated
A sample-to-sample Euclidean distance heatmap on vst values annotated by condition
An explicit verdict on sample_01 (keep or remove) with a stated reason grounded in the library size, detected genes, PCA, and distance results; no silent exclusion
All sample identifiers in the QC outputs match the 12 rows of metadata.csv

plan.title: AD lesional vs control: pre-test sample QC
plan.analytical_narrative: The user asks how the twelve skin samples (6 atopic dermatitis lesional vs 6 control) look before any testing: library sizes, a PCA, sample-to-sample distances, and a verdict on the shallow sample. The profiled inputs are gene-level raw counts from Salmon (12000 x 13 counts.csv) plus a 12 x 2 metadata table, one batch, no known batch structure, and one flagged concern: sample_01 sits about 4x below the median library size. Because the counts are raw Salmon output with no statement of length correction, and because the question stops at sample structure, the plan is a single grounded QC step: import the counts, compute library sizes and detected genes, apply a blind variance stabilizing transformation, and produce a PCA on the 500 most variable genes plus a Euclidean sample-distance heatmap, each colored by condition. The shallow sample is kept throughout, inspected on every plot, and given an explicit keep/remove verdict with a stated reason — removal is a judgment, not a default, since downstream count models down-weight it through its size factor. No differential expression, enrichment, or modeling is planned: it is unasked scope for this question.

steps.method: DESeq2 blind vst sample structure QC (library sizes, PCA on top-variance genes, sample distance heatmap, low-depth sample verdict)
